source: Loom's status record, maintained in the repository and checked against main

items.label: Transient model failure recovery
items.detail: Since 0.4.0: at most three identical model attempts before any stream output, with per-attempt metrics and no effect retries. Persistent provider overload reports Unavailable.

items.label: System time queries
items.detail: Since 0.4.0: task install builds the current checkout; system-query@1 reads the host clock, verifies its observation and completes without a workspace or confinement.

items.label: Custom protocol sources
items.detail: Since 0.4.0: shared catalogs, local snapshots and pinned Git installation. Offline verified loading. Unreleased: b10x-loom run --action-bindings binds an installed protocol's actions to operator-declared commands (argv, no shell, arguments as JSON on stdin, report as JSON on stdout); otherwise executable bindings remain host supplied.

items.label: Bounded working context
items.detail: Since 0.4.0: opt-in CLI policy with typed working state, retrievable history, bounded requests and payload-free measurements. Legacy remains default pending matched live quality and cost evaluation.

items.label: Stored result references
items.detail: Since 0.3.0: bounded result previews and exact reference-based edit composition, resolved before admission. Run-local storage; live quality and token-cost savings remain unmeasured.

items.label: b10x-loom run
items.detail: Routes an intent to a protocol, opens a governed case and runs it until it is blocked, printing each step and the stop reason. Exit 0 for a verified completed query or at the human merge gate; 3 for another stopped run. Completed a live run against a hosted model on 2026-10-05.

items.label: b10x-loom plugin run slack-handler
items.detail: Unreleased: the slack-handler plugin (b10x-loom-plugin-slack) walks the Slack channels the bot is a member of through the Connectors command line, read only, and hands the plugin host the messages nobody answered, mentions first: aged min_age_minutes, no thread reply but the poster's, no bot message, no system message, no reaction by the bot. A question gets a proposed reply read from the configured data sources, a task a proposed case; nothing is sent. --once runs one cycle; plugin report prints one line per proposal. Tested on recorded responses and a fake connectors only; no live run yet.

items.label: b10x-loom-sdk
items.detail: One crate that re-exports Commission's contracts and runtime, the executor, the governor and intake. Its example runs a whole embedding on scripted fake models.

items.label: SDK stability
items.detail: Unreleased: one page names the stable surface of b10x-loom-sdk, every port a host implements with its loom_sdk path and every loom_sdk path control-plane imports, stable within a release line with each break named in CHANGELOG.md; a compile witness implements every listed port through loom_sdk alone.

items.label: Source releases at version tags
items.detail: 0.23.0 is the current release (0.1.0 was the first): a bare-version tag the release workflow verifies against the workspace version and CHANGELOG.md, with a GitHub Release. Consumers pin tag = "0.23.0".

items.label: A release on a registry
items.detail: Nothing is on a registry; consumers depend on a release tag.

items.label: Commission's runtime loop
items.detail: run_until_blocked drives a commission over its ports until the run stops: approval gate (a step performed under an authority grant passes it), nothing performable, authority needed, step budget, or 64 steps without a budget.

items.label: Revalidation before every effect
items.detail: Each proposal becomes an action request bound to the frontier's revision and is rechecked against the current frontier, case revision and authority provider.

items.label: Commission makes the effect call
items.detail: Admitted requests go to the embedder's EffectPort once; the case moves only after a Performed effect (Atlas ADR 0082).

items.label: Concurrent reads in one step
items.detail: Unreleased: an executor proposes up to 16 reads at once (ExecutorOutcome::ProposedReads). The runtime admits them only when the effect port reads every one and the frontier lists each admissible with no authority, else invokes nothing; each read is revalidated, the admitted ones run concurrently, each once through its binding, and are recorded in the order proposed. A fan-out is one step. Writes, and actions that need authority, stay one per iteration; no model executor proposes a fan-out yet.

items.label: Suspend on an approval, resume after a restart
items.detail: Unreleased: given a suspension port the host implements, run_with_suspension suspends a Run whose request needs authority the provider withholds and stores the commission's Suspension; resume_after_grant takes it, performs the request once, in a new process if need be, after the grant, and releases it, and refuses when the case revision moved. The take and the release name the request the resume revalidated: of two resumes racing over one Suspension one performs the request and the other is refused, and a resume that read a Suspension since resumed and replaced for another request is refused, naming both, and performs nothing. A resume that stopped after the take leaves the request in doubt: every later resume is refused and performs nothing, and settling it is the host's. A commission holding a Suspension starts no new Run with a port. run_until_blocked, with no port, is unchanged. loom_governor::FileSuspensionStore keeps the Suspension in a directory, beside the case store and under its lock. b10x-loom run --state <DIR> keeps the case, the Suspension and the commission's resume context in that directory and runs the commission through run_with_suspension, so a run stopped for an approval leaves a Pending Suspension. b10x-loom approve writes a grant for the request that Suspension holds and performs nothing; b10x-loom resume performs it once through resume_after_grant, a granted repository.merge as a merge hand-off record that moves no Git ref, once per HEAD of a commission and only at the HEAD the case holds, and runs on; a merge the agent proposes again at a HEAD the commission already handed off holds no Suspension, since the host answers its hold settled; a commit made after the Suspension is refused CaseMoved, a run that stops at its gate holding nothing says so and exits 4, and each refusal of a resume has its own exit status.

items.label: Connector effect port
items.detail: Unreleased: b10x-loom-connectors fills Commission's ConnectorInvoker over a Connectors v0.35.0 service. It invokes the bound operation once on the host's endpoint for its instance and answers Performed with the attempt Connectors recorded for a write or the audit record it completed for a read, Refused only when Connectors reports the attempt refused or not attempted, and an error otherwise. Whether a released Connectors provider offers file-edit and test-run operations is not known yet.

items.label: Mandate authority provider
items.detail: Unreleased, opt-in: b10x-loom-mandate answers Commission's authority port with Mandate v0.9.0's check, over Mandate ports the host builds it with. The subject is the Mandate verified context the host puts in the commission's authority context, the capability is the action and the case the resource. An allow is a grant, an approval requirement suspends the run as the approval gate does, a refusal is a denial, and a Mandate outage or an authority context that is no Mandate context grants nothing. b10x-loom approve and resume use it behind --mandate; run does not.

items.label: Mandate approval on resume
items.detail: Unreleased, opt-in: b10x-loom approve --mandate <FILE> records a Mandate approval of the held request in the state directory's approval log, and resume --mandate <FILE> performs the request only when Mandate v0.9.0's check_with_approval clears and consumes it, keeping the consumption before anything is performed. A second resume with the same approval, an expired approval and a grant naming none are refused and perform nothing, and resume without --mandate refuses a grant naming an approval. FILE is host-trusted; Loom configures Mandate from it over Mandate's in-memory ports until Mandate ships a policy adapter. Tested on local fixtures only; no live run.

items.label: Plugin host
items.detail: Unreleased: b10x-loom-plugin hosts a plugin in a loop: poll, classify, project, a governed read-only turn on inbound-answer@1 over Connectors data sources, and one record line per handled item. A reply is a proposal in the record and is never sent. b10x-loom plugin run hosts the one registered plugin, slack-handler.

items.label: Substrate effect port
items.detail: Not decided. The local adapter embeds Substrate for tests.

items.label: Commission's contracts stay independent
items.detail: b10x-loom-commission depends on no Loom executor, no Canon and no model-provider crate; task commission:deps-guard fails the gate if it does.

items.label: Loom implements Commission's AgentExecutor
items.detail: A step projects the frontier, selects over that catalogue, asks Commission's admission check, generates arguments and ends at a ProposedAction. Loom invokes nothing and never suspends for authority.

items.label: Loom revalidates its selection before proposing
items.detail: With Loom::with_governor, a step reads the case's current frontier from the governor once after the selection and proposes nothing for a selection made at another case revision or of an action that frontier's catalogue does not list. A selection made at a revision the case has left is reported to Commission as CaseMoved, and run_until_blocked judges the run on the case's current frontier. Opt-in: b10x-loom run does not enable it yet.

items.label: Workflow definitions
items.detail: Unreleased: WorkflowExecutor runs a loom.workflow definition over a catalog protocol. Deterministic steps propose their action and literal arguments with no model call; a judgement step asks the model only among its own actions. A step the frontier does not list ends NeedsHumanJudgment, a step advances only once performed, and Commission revalidates every proposal. A step declares typed outputs from its performed report, and a later step's arguments name them: the runtime fills them in with no model call, and an absent or mistyped output proposes nothing and ends NeedsHumanJudgment. A judgement step lists the earlier outputs it is given: their values reach its instructions as a typed data block, never as instructions, and a listed output the run did not produce asks the model nothing. Given a run store (the governor's FileWorkflowRunStore, or the host's own), the run's record is written after every performed step, and resume(run_id) continues the run in another process, after an approval or a crash, with every output bound and its usage report covering every segment.

items.label: Per-run model usage report
items.detail: RunMeter, MeteredModelPort and MeteredExecutor count every ModelPort turn of a Commission run, failed turns included, and report the calls, the provider's tokens and the cost at a declared rate card per executor call and in total (loom.metering.RunUsageReport). A cost no card priced is absent, never zero.

items.label: Selections outside the catalogue are refused
items.detail: The catalogue lists only actions Commission admission does not refuse. An action id it does not list is refused whatever its confidence, and no arguments are generated.

items.label: Model-backed selector and argument generator
items.detail: The slice's ModelSelector and ModelArguments use forced tool calls through llm, told the intent, its references and a bounded transcript. Since 0.3.0, argument generation can retrieve stored results before returning an action.

items.label: Arguments for the selected action only
items.detail: A generator is handed the selected catalogue entry only, and the request for arguments is recorded against its selection.

items.label: Schema validation of arguments
items.detail: Where an action schema comes from is not decided.

items.label: Fast typed and hybrid selectors; confidence fallback
A confidence fallback is recorded as two linked selections
items.detail: Unreleased: when the hybrid selector falls back, Loom records the fast selection as Overruled, naming the stronger selector's selection that replaced it, and that selection; each carries its own selector's strategy, and only the replacement reaches argument generation and revalidation.

items.label: Selection telemetry for Metaharness
items.detail: Unreleased: every selection gets one SelectionRecord (strategy, candidate count, chosen action, confidence, latency, tokens the selector reported, and on an overruled fast selection the strategy it fell back to), read with Loom::selection_records; a governed run's session counts the selections refused at the execution boundary after they were made (boundary_refusals). Neither is evidence.

items.label: Canon governor
items.detail: CanonGovernor evaluates a case's engineering protocol with Canon on every frontier and completion; no clock, network or model call, and no invented authority.

items.label: Hosted governor contracts
items.detail: Since 0.2.0: host-admitted Canon protocols, trusted freshness callback and fallible case storage. No database backend or automatic protocol adoption.

items.label: Case inputs from the host
items.detail: Unreleased: a software-change@1 case opens with risk, change_kind and affects_security_boundary, given by the host (b10x-loom run --risk, --change-kind, --affects-security-boundary) and never by a model; an undeclared input, an unlisted value or a missing one is refused before anything is stored, and an obligation the inputs do not select is not open.

items.label: Evidence that order and age rules decide
items.detail: Unreleased: the slice submits an implementation_change for every committed edit and, on a bugfix, a regression_test_result beside each test result after its first tests.write that committed; every record carries the host clock's observed_at and the trusted producer, so a bugfix that runs its regression test red before its edit discharges red_first.required, and b10x-loom's governor evaluates at the host instant, so an observation past its max_age no longer applies.

items.label: A regression result runs the written test
items.detail: Unreleased: a bugfix's regression_test_result comes only from b10x-loom run --regression-test-command <CMD>, run once per test path the run's tests.write committed with {path} filled, never from the suite; without it no run is a regression result. The governor takes a record's observed_at only as the instant of the observation it cites and received, and refuses the record otherwise.

items.label: Stateless evaluation
items.detail: loom_governor::evaluate and b10x-loom evaluate decide a catalog protocol over a caller's canon-case/1 snapshot and canon-evidence/1 records, with an optional trusted time, and return Canon's decision as JSON; no Commission type, no case store, no clock. An unusable input is refused naming it.

items.label: Intent references
items.detail: Tracker keys, chat permalinks, merge and pull requests and URLs, extracted in order without a model.

items.label: Protocol router
items.detail: A model picks from the shared catalog of engineering, Loom and explicitly installed custom definitions; a pick outside it or below the threshold is refused.

items.label: Local slice for software-change@1
items.detail: Edits, inspects and tests a git work tree; evidence only from the test command's exit status; never merges, pushes or deploys. Tests use Substrate by default since 0.2.0.

items.label: Catalog route models
items.detail: b10x-loom run --catalog <PATH> reads an llm catalog; --model and --classifier-model then name its route aliases, built through llm's catalog-to-Model port, so a self-hosted endpoint can drive a run. An unknown alias or an unreadable catalog stops before any model call.

items.label: Run event stream
items.detail: b10x-loom run --output jsonl writes one JSON record per line, each with schema_version 1: the route, model turns, tool calls, reported usage, approvals, and one terminal record last whose exit_status is the process exit status. Human output stays the default.

items.label: Executors for other protocols
items.detail: An incident-response slice is on the plan. The CLI executes software-change@1, clock-compatible query protocols and, with --action-bindings, installed protocols whose actions are bound to commands; an unbound action stops with NoLocalExecutor.

items.label: Run model generated from ESS
items.detail: Session, Turn, ActionCatalogue, Selection and ArgumentRequest are synthesized from ess/ and re-exported; Commission's model likewise from ess/commission/.

items.label: ESS hard gate
items.detail: task check fails unless loom and commission validate strictly, compile, synthesize with no refusals and carry no open question; intake's system validates.

items.label: Commission's ESS conformance suite
items.detail: b10x-loom-commission passes the suite synthesized from ess/commission/.

items.label: Loom's ESS conformance suite
items.detail: b10x-loom-executor passes the suite synthesized from ess/, run by task conform; the target answers RevalidateSelection's external not-in-frontier branch, and an executor test holds the membership rule.

items.label: Harness modules ported
items.detail: The provider wires, messages, responses, HTTP and the turn loop of Harness, as modules of b10x-loom-executor. JSON from a model or provider nested deeper than 128 levels is refused with a typed error.

items.label: Sessions, transcripts and streaming
items.detail: The session module runs the ported loop and files its session outside the workspace (directory 0700, file 0600), up to its last completed turn, with no credential and no instruction text; a filed session is resumed by id. Streamed deltas reach the sink as they arrive. Not yet called from a governed run.

items.label: Harness loop wired to a governed run
items.detail: Loom::run_loop, and LoopExecutor behind Commission's AgentExecutor port, run the ported loop on one frontier: each turn's tool list is the catalogue projected from the governor's current frontier, a model's call of a catalogue action is selected, given its arguments and revalidated before Loom proposes it, a call outside the catalogue is refused to the model by name, and each completed turn is recorded. Each compaction of the run's session is recorded with the usage the endpoint reported for its summary request; the request after it keeps the standing instruction and carries the current frontier's catalogue. Loom::interrupt cancels a run and leaves its session Interrupted with nothing proposed, and Loom::resume_loop resumes a session by id from the approval checkpoint its run stopped at, projecting from the frontier current at resume and revalidating before anything is proposed: a merge awaiting its approval is proposed again without asking the model while the case has not moved, and a held call made at an earlier revision is never proposed. Checkpoints are held in memory. A budget of the loop that binds (turns, input or output tokens, cost, wall time, or a ceiling it could no longer observe) suspends the run for it, as SuspensionReason::LoopBudget carrying the loop's stop, through LoopExecutor and a workflow's judgement step alike. b10x-loom run does not use it yet.
